video.title: The Best Way to Clone These $1M+ Online Businesses (Legally)

summary: Chris Koerner shows how to reverse engineer businesses built on HighLevel, a white label platform, by reviewing their websites, prices, ads and history. He examines software for real estate agents, event rental companies and general sales and marketing, then lists tools for researching other businesses. His main takeaway is to study proven offers and acquisition methods, then build an original version for a specific market or partner with someone who already has an audience. The video includes hypothetical revenue calculations and affiliate promotion for HighLevel.

tactics.name: Reverse engineer a digital business from public evidence
steps: Find businesses on an award list, marketplace or other public directory.
Search the company name on Google and review its current website, offer, features and testimonials.
Check the Meta Ads Library for active advertising.
Use the Wayback Machine to compare the current site with earlier versions and see how pricing and positioning changed.
Use public information to form hypotheses about acquisition, customer count and revenue; label estimates as estimates.

quote.text: Because their pricing may have started out as a flat fee, or as $10 a month, or as $1,000 a month. We need to see how they learned
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Reduce friction in a niche software offer
steps: Identify the extra work customers must do after buying software.
Add setup, useful data or a ready-made workflow when it removes that work.
Sell the outcome and time saved, not only the software features.
Make the product easier to start using and harder to leave by providing continuing value.

quote.text: This is them strategically removing friction, which is a first principle. It's what you want to do in any business in any setting.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Partner with an existing creator instead of building an audience first
steps: Find a creator who already serves the intended niche but does not already sell or use the product.
Offer to build and operate the software, handle fulfillment and customer service, and share revenue.
Use the creator's audience to test demand before investing in audience building.
The host suggests trying less crowded social channels for outreach; check applicable consent rules before sending UK marketing DMs.

quote.text: You build this same thing, partner with them, and say, "Hey, I built this awesome SMS automation platform
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Keep a proven price rather than undercutting automatically
steps: Review how long the existing price has been used.
If the offer and price appear stable, test the value proposition before lowering the price.
Avoid assuming that a competitor's $97 monthly price should become $77 with a smaller setup fee.

quote.text: If I were you copying this, I would not change the pricing. This sounds like it's the sweet spot.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Test a charity-backed guarantee
steps: Offer a specific refund or charity donation if a customer does not like the product after a stated trial period.
State the amount and timing clearly.
The example offers a $100 check or $150 donation after a site has been live for 90 days.

quote.text: If you don't love our software after your site has been live for 90 days, we'll give you a check for $100
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Consider a lifetime price for flat-cost software
steps: Compare a recurring subscription with a lifetime offer.
A lifetime offer may stand out when the underlying platform fee does not rise with each additional customer.
Account for long-term service and support obligations before choosing a one-time price.

quote.text: So, a lifetime price makes sense when you're white-labeling software that's a flat fee, no matter how many sub accounts, aka customers that you have.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Study ad longevity and test new creative
steps: Look at how long a competitor's active ads have been running.
Treat a long-running ad as a possible sign that the creative is working, while recognizing that the company may simply not be monitoring it.
Test simple static creative against short videos that show a before-and-after outcome.

quote.text: And sometimes simple text, transparent background, stock photo ads work. Usually video ads work even better.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Use specialist research tools and lower-cost access
steps: Use BuiltWith or Wappalyzer to identify website technology.
Use SimilarWeb for traffic estimates and Sensor Tower for app download estimates.
Use review sites such as G2 to identify product gaps.
Compare the cost of a paid research account with hiring someone who already has access for a small, specific task.

quote.text: Total life hack. If you want to know how much traffic a website gets, SimilarWeb. That is the only one.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Use competitor reviews and hiring activity as product research
steps: Collect software reviews and summarize what customers say the product is missing.
Review a competitor's job listings for mentions of upcoming products, features or initiatives.
Use the findings to choose a product gap to test.

quote.text: G2 is the best for that. Bombora, b o m b o r a, is also really good for stuff like that.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Track changes to competitor websites
steps: Choose a competitor page or price that matters.
Set a website-change monitor to alert you when the page changes.
Use the alerts to review new prices, products or availability.

quote.text: Or you want to see if your competitors' pricing changes at any point, you can use something like Distill, Visual Ping, or Change Tower
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

evidence_quality.rationale: The host reverse engineers businesses from publicly visible websites, ads and third-party tools rather than interviewing the operators or inspecting their accounts. He provides useful process examples and some specific prices, but many customer counts, revenue figures and margins are estimates or hypothetical calculations.
evidence_quality.promotional_conflict: The host says he is a HighLevel affiliate, offers an affiliate link with an extended free trial, and promotes his TK Owners community.
